assets.prompt: Create one production atlas of SIX separate square mini illustrations for a first-grade Chinese comprehension quiz in the lesson 《小小的船》. Overall 3:2 landscape, exactly three equal columns and two equal rows. The unseen tile edges must lie at exact thirds of width and half height. Clean flat uniform warm cream at all tile edges and in the gutters. Each panel is an independent square mini scene with 12% padding, so that cropping produces six complete images. No borders, lettering, numbers, arrows, watermarks, decorative icons or panel labels. The picture-book style is matte gouache with fine paper grain, clear paper-cut shapes, warm cream, pine green, apricot and persimmon, quiet low-saturation indigo only at night. All subjects must remain unambiguous at a 96px thumbnail. TOP ROW is three nearly identical front-three-quarter-overhead studies with the same low wide open woven apricot basket and one tiny red-rim round drum. Repeat the basket camera and centered size exactly across all three. Left: the small drum is BESIDE the basket to its right, fully outside, each object contacting the ground separately. Middle: the drum is BEHIND the basket, slightly right, its lower third hidden by the back wall of the basket, but the entire oval opening is visible empty. Right: drum sits entirely INSIDE the basket, below its upper rim, with the basket wall and surrounding inner space visibly enclosing it. No drumsticks. BOTTOM ROW is three original distinct mini scenes using the same short-black-haired child in an apricot coat. Left: the child on a quiet riverbank unmistakably tilts head and gaze DOWN toward pale star-like reflections on the dark water below; visible shoreline and absolutely no stars above the head. Middle: the child unmistakably gazes UP at two clearly white clouds in a bright blue DAY sky, no stars. Right: a warm interior with a recognizable window, the child unmistakably tips the face UP toward several clear stars in the dark blue NIGHT sky beyond the window, no water or clouds. For the bottom three panels, keep head and eye direction clearly legible, use side profiles and simple shapes. Do not let any object touch any tile margin.
